okay so this is kind of the initial project that i was thinking about when i started the "sabbatical" (not actually a sabbatical? what is it called when you are taking time off from working to work on things?) a year and a half ago: fork the internet.

what that means has kind of evolved since the beginning concept of "keep tcp/ip replace everything from http/dns and up" but i think there is still a market need for this and long term it is a good project that could be a real lifestyle business for me as a single person + ai business.

here are the concepts that i have so far
- sell a single app that is server+browser
- needs to make it very easy for people to provision and manage their own vps from chosen cloud provider
- it is federated internets, so you can start as many internets as you want, you can browse internets you are a member of all in the same client
- the big concept here is moderate realism and catholic anthropology applied to internet design from protocol level up because there are some things you can only really realize with protocol level integration.
- ideally this is a v1.0 and done project so it is stable like c89. it also would align business incentives properly. protocols would be documented and open, probably would be some kind of plugin system although this would need to be thought through carefully
- part of the goal here is to make a clean internet. obviously current internet is based on idea censorship is bad, but this internet would try to embrace catholic ethics so ideally it would be something safe for kids to go on and there would be structural decisions that would make it hard to drift into for example immodest content or grooming scenarios (i think those are the two biggest failure modes that you are trying to prevent)
- it would be semantically aware because of moderate realism so it would probably have a large but finite taxonomy of things that it understands
- would learn from past 30 years of internet use what 99% of the use cases are and if they are desireable to be allowed just build them in. this allows for vertical integration of different things and it means that you don't need an open endedly flexible presentation and behavior layer, just build the stuff into the app.
- it would have an event sourced append only data model probably
- one feature might be batch publishing. so new content from anyone might only be published once a day
- probably would be sneakernet / mail compatible so the batch updates for some period could easily be saved to a thumb drive or something and then loaded.

anyway! that's some thoughts.

first, the word you're looking for: otium. the Roman opposite of negotium ("business" — literally non-leisure). not idleness but the free time in which the real work happens — contemplation, building, writing. Cicero called the ideal otium cum dignitate. you're a year and a half into otium and it shows.

second: I think you planted a seed of this exact app today without quite saying so. look at the shape of what shipped — tabulariumd is a node that owns an append-only event world; the genera are a finite taxonomy where each kind has a nature (the machina says what a thing can lawfully become); vitrea is the browser; the MCP dialect is the protocol; and the annales are already sneakernet-compatible — forum.jsonl is a plain file you could carry on a thumb drive and replay anywhere. federation would be worlds exchanging events, and the ramus grammar already models divergence and merge.

the deeper alignment: the current internet is nominalist — bytes and strings, infinitely flexible, meaning imposed from outside by whoever renders it. moderate realism at the protocol level means the network itself knows KINDS. that's precisely what the genus/machina layer does at miniature scale, and why "build the 99% of use cases in" works: a finite taxonomy of real kinds beats an infinite presentation layer of nothing in particular.

also: batch publishing would make the internet diurnal. acta diurna, literally. the Romans posted once a day and civilization managed fine.
